To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
combined GSTM1-null/GSTA1*A/*A genotypes might be used as genetic markers for predicting cardiovascular death risk in end-stage renal patients.
combined GSTM1-null/GSTA1*B/*B genotypes might be associated with lower overall and cardiovascular mortality in comparison with combined GSTM-null/GSTA1*A/*A genotypes in ESRD.
GSTM1*null and GSTA1*B variants are independently associated with the risk of death from cardiovascular disease in ESRD.

the role of genetic polymorphisms in GSTA1 and GSTM1 genes on the risk of cardiovascular mortality and the risk of cardiovascular disease in general in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) and on hemodialysis.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the GSTM1*1/GSTA1*B/*B genotypes are associated with a lower risk of cardiovascular death, whereas GSTM1*2/GSTA1*A/*A are associated with a higher risk of death.
the presence of GSTM1-null genotype in combination with GSTA1*A gene variant might be considered as a risk factor for death from cardiovascular disease in ESRD population.
the association between GSTM-null genotype and overall and cardiovascular mortality is not significant after multiple testing corrections.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GSTM1*1/GSTA1*B/*B genotypes are associated with a decreased cardiovascular mortality in ESDR patients.
the GSTM1*GSTM1*0/GSTT1*GSTT1*1 genotype is associated with increased risk of cardiovascular death in hemodialysis patients.
ESRD patients carrying GSTM1*active and GSTA1*B genotypes may have better prognosis than those with GSTM-null and GSTA1-A genotypes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
GSTM1*null genotype is associated with higher mortality in ESRDs patients.
the presence of GSTA1*A gene variant may modify the effect of GSTM deletion polymorphism on the risk of cardiovascular outcomes in hemodialysed patients.
GSTM1-null genotype may not be a good predictor of cardiovascular death risk in patients undergoing hemodialyses.
